author: YUAN X
scope: four-slice/six-line carrier residuals, tetrahedral symmetry, double-Pell finite arithmetic, and conditional positive-series acceleration
publication_source: PR #1136 on publication/yuan-x-tetrahedral-residuals-20260903; not yet canonical main

formalization_evidence.canonicality_note: Lean-checked proof evidence is currently PR/branch-backed. This ledger extracts theorem statements and evidence; it does not by itself promote those source branches to Foundation or claim they are already merged into main.

theorems.hypotheses: four declared slice labels with six shared unoriented line-family labels in the Enterprise FCC carrier readout
theorems.statement: The four slice labels and six line-family labels have exactly the vertex-edge incidence of K4: every slice contains three line families, every line family belongs to two slices, and every distinct slice pair shares exactly one line family.
theorems.boundary: This does not identify the six carrier line families with the six native P000 spatial axes.

theorems.hypotheses: V0={v in Z^4: sum v_i=0}, E0={x in Z^6: sum x_e=0}, delta(v)_ij=v_i+v_j
theorems.statement: The residual quotient E0/delta(V0) has constructive coordinates (p,q,epsilon) and is isomorphic as an abelian group to Z^2 direct-sum Z/2Z, equivalently to A2(Z) direct-sum Z/2Z.
theorems.classification: Two zero-total edge states are delta-equivalent iff their opposite-edge matching sums agree and their first-three-edge sums have even difference.

theorems.hypotheses: same integer endpoint-sum quotient as EMTR-T02
theorems.statement: tau=(1,0,0,0,0,-1) is not in delta(V0), while 2 tau is in delta(V0); hence tau represents the nonzero order-two residual class.

theorems.hypotheses: extend the same endpoint-sum system from integers to real coefficients
theorems.statement: Over R the parity obstruction disappears, the residual quotient is R^2, and the two integer sheets distinguished by epsilon collapse to one real residual class.
theorems.interpretation: division by two supplies the lift that is integrally obstructed; real completion retains the free A2 directions and erases the order-two residual.

theorems.hypotheses: the K4 carrier incidence of EMTR-T01 and any permutation of the four slice labels
theorems.statement: Every slice permutation induces the corresponding line-family permutation and the endpoint-sum map is equivariant under simultaneous slice and line transport.

theorems.hypotheses: the mod-two residual normal coordinates induced by EMTR-T02 and the tetrahedral S4 action
theorems.statement: The torsion line is S4-invariant, but there is no additive torsion retraction invariant under the three adjacent transpositions. Equivalently, the invariant two-torsion line has no S4-equivariant additive complement in the residual mod-two module.
theorems.hidden_rotation_witness: A double transposition can fix the free pair while translating the torsion coordinate by a free-coordinate parity.
theorems.boundary: This is a concrete finite-module nonsplitting theorem; it is not promoted here to a universal native holonomy theorem.

theorems.statement: The eight residual states identify with Aff(F2^2,F2) by f_(p,q,e)(x,y)=e+px+qy. The six nonconstant affine functions have two-point supports and correspond bijectively to the six K4 edges; addition of the nonzero constant complements support and exchanges opposite edges.
theorems.boundary: The manuscript proof is finite and explicit; a coordinate-free Lean equivalence is the next formal packaging target.

theorems.hypotheses: u is invertible in a field and (u+u^-1)/2=P^2
theorems.interpretation: An exact square half-trace forces a paired positive/negative quadratic shell factorization.

theorems.hypotheses: P=99 with the displayed integer witnesses
theorems.consequence: The principal integers in Ramanujan's N=58 expression admit a common exact Pell/arithmetic certificate.
theorems.boundary: These identities do not derive the classical Ramanujan modular identity.

theorems.hypotheses: nonzero scale and nonzero target coefficients in a characteristic-zero field
theorems.statement: A source coefficient can be exactly rewritten as scale^-1*n*target_n*scaledPrecision_n, and finite weighted generating sums preserve this identity term by term.
theorems.role: finite algebraic bridge from a slow precision coefficient sequence to a weighted generating functional; no infinite-series theorem is assumed.

theorems.hypotheses: positive initial term and nonnegative series terms, with the next term strictly positive
theorems.statement: Partial sums strictly increase and their reciprocals strictly decrease. If a finite partial sum lies below an exact positive inverse period, its reciprocal lies above that period.
theorems.ramanujan_boundary: Identifying the exact inverse period with 1/pi for the N=58 series uses the classical Ramanujan-CM identity as an external analytic input.

theorems.statement: Every finite omitted tail is bounded by first_omitted/(1-q); the N=58 specialization has q_58=25/99^4=25/96059601.
theorems.boundary: The ratio certificate controls the positive tail once the relevant series representation is supplied; it does not prove that representation.

theorems.hypotheses: k>=2, m>=1, and 0<=s<=k-1 in the parameter range of the k to k+2m balance comparison
theorems.statement: The nontrivial middle-prefix majorization numerator m*(k*(m+1+2s)-2s*(s+1)) is strictly positive; equivalently the corresponding rational middle-prefix difference is positive.
theorems.boundary: This ledger records the finite arithmetic core. Any Gamma-convexity or asymptotic pi^m completion theorem must cite its separate analytic proof status.

negative_boundaries.statement: The FCC six line-family carrier readout is not identified here with the six native P000 spatial axes.
The classical N=58 Ramanujan-CM identity is not derived from the finite carrier, residual quotient, or Pell certificates in this package.
The affine-function model EMTR-T07 is proved in the manuscript but its coordinate-free Lean equivalence is not yet part of the accepted formal stack.
